name: Eyeshadow neutral (brow bone)

card.summary: A matte neutral eyeshadow dabbed on the brow bone to add soft shading and definition that makes the eye area look deeper-set.
card.aka: brow bone shading, neutral brow-bone shadow
card.note: Cosmetic and removable; results depend on skin tone and technique.

quick.overview:
Neutral brow-bone eyeshadow is a matte, skin-tone-adjacent shade placed under or along the brow and brow bone. It adds gentle shading so the area around the eye looks more defined.

It matters to looksmaxxers because eye-area depth and brow-bone projection are part of how the upper face is assessed. Makeup gives a temporary, non-surgical version of that look. Very little published research addresses it specifically.
quick.how: Users apply a matte shadow a shade or two deeper than their skin along the brow bone and blend it, often with a brush. The effect is removed with makeup remover and reapplied as wanted.
quick.risks: As a topical cosmetic it can cause irritation or allergic reactions in some users, and eye-area products should be labelled for that use. Its effect is cosmetic and temporary.

lead: Neutral brow-bone eyeshadow is a matte, natural-toned shadow used to shade the brow bone and the upper eye socket. By adding contour it can make the eye area appear deeper-set and more defined, which some people use to change the look of the upper face without surgery. It is an application of the broader makeup technique of contouring, in which shades darker than the skin make areas recede and lighter ones read as prominent [1].

The brow ridge is the bony crest above the eye sockets, and Wikipedia describes it as a trait linked to sexual dimorphism that is typically more prominent in men than in women [2]. In appearance communities the area is discussed mostly in terms of projection, brow tilt and surgery; makeup is the temporary, reversible counterpart to those discussions. Makeup brands and artists give differing advice on the area: some guides for deep-set eyes recommend brightening the lid so the brow bone does not overshadow the eye, while a guide to masculine contouring suggests a small amount of muted shadow beneath the front of the brow and into the socket for a stronger facial plane [3][4].
No published trials of brow-bone eyeshadow are listed. Information comes from the makeup literature and brand guides, and from general sources on cosmetics and eyeshadow formulation [5][6].

chain: Matte shadow darkens the brow-bone area slightly

angle.text: Applying a neutral matte shade along the brow bone creates shadow that suggests depth. It is temporary and removed with makeup remover.

paras: The product is an ordinary matte powder or cream eyeshadow in a skin-toned or soft brown shade. Used along the brow bone it works as contour: darker areas recede and lighter areas read as prominent [1]. Wikipedia describes eye shadow as available in powder, liquid, pencil, cream and mousse forms, built from base fillers such as mica, talc and kaolin, binders, slip agents and preservatives, and notes that it can also be applied under the eyes, on the cheeks or on the brow bones [6].

The brow ridge separates the forehead from the roof of the eye socket, with the eyebrows resting on its lower margin, and varies across populations; Wikipedia reports that it is more prominent in men on average [2]. A prominent ridge and a deep-set eye are related impressions: L'Oreal Paris's guide to deep-set eyes says the brow bone can overshadow the eyes and lids and suggests brightening the lid area, with shimmer bringing the eyes forward [3].

Because eyeshadow works with light and shadow rather than bone, it changes how the area looks in a photograph or face-to-face rather than the structure itself. Users who want more depth add shadow; users who want the eye to look more open add light.

The general contouring approach places a shade one or two tones darker than the skin where shadow is wanted and a lighter shade where projection is wanted, and blending is the finishing step [1][6]. For the brow bone, one makeup-brand guide to masculine contouring suggests a small amount of cool-toned contour or muted shadow beneath the front of the brow and into the socket, blended so the result reads as natural depth rather than visible makeup [4]. The same guide describes lower, more horizontal brows as giving a stronger expression and recommends softer contour and less contrast for everyday wear [4].

Wikipedia's eyeshadow article names flat brushes for packing colour, fluffy tapered brushes for blending and dense or angled brushes for precision, and says blending is the most important step; products are removed with makeup remover, water and soap or wipes [6].

Brow-bone shape is a recurring topic in appearance forums, usually in relation to surgery such as implants and to the idea of brow tilt. Makeup is described in this context as a reversible alternative for people who want to try a deeper-set look before considering anything permanent. Wikipedia reports that men use makeup to enhance features or cover blemishes and dark circles, and that stigma around men wearing makeup in the United States has eased in the 21st century [5].

Wikipedia traces contouring to Elizabethan stage actors using chalk and soot, to Max Factor's shading for screen faces in the 1930s and 1940s and to Kevyn Aucoin's sculpted looks and 2000 book Face Forward, with heavier contouring popularised in the 2010s by celebrities such as Kim Kardashian [1]. Eye makeup is older: Wikipedia dates eye paints to predynastic Egypt and says Elizabeth Arden introduced eye shadow in her US salons in 1914, with the term becoming standard in the 1930s [6].

Wikipedia's cosmetics article reports that in the US cosmetics and their ingredients do not need FDA approval before sale, except colour additives, and that manufacturers must ensure their products are safe; in the EU Regulation EC 1223/2009 requires a responsible person and a product information file [5]. Fragrances, preservatives and some emulsifiers are among the common contact allergens in cosmetics, and the skin around the eyes is described as thin and sensitive [5]. A historical example of an eye product hazard is the early 20th century mascara Lash Lure, which caused blindness [5].

timeline.event: Elizabethan stage actors use chalk and soot so audiences can read facial expressions, an early form of facial shading [1]
Elizabeth Arden introduces eye shadow in her US salons [6]
Eye shadow becomes the common industry name and Max Factor adds shading to screen faces [6][1]
Max Factor Sr. presents a tutorial for contouring different face shapes [1]
Kevyn Aucoin's book Face Forward introduces sculpted contouring to the general public [1]
Celebrities such as Kim Kardashian popularise heavier contouring and brands sell dedicated contour products [1]

lore.intro: Brow-bone depth is discussed in appearance communities as part of upper-face assessment, and makeup guides give differing advice on whether to shade or brighten the area [3][4].

claims.claim: Matte shading on the brow bone makes the eyes look deeper-set and more defined
claims.believers: Makeup guides for masculine contouring recommend muted shadow beneath the front of the brow and into the socket for a stronger facial plane [4].
claims.experts: No published study has tested brow-bone shading; Wikipedia describes contouring as using shades darker than the skin to create shadow and lighter ones to project areas forward [1].

claims.claim: Brightening the lid is the better way to deal with a heavy brow bone
claims.believers: A mainstream beauty guide says a prominent brow bone can overshadow the eyes and recommends a light lid shade and shimmer to bring the eyes forward [3].
claims.experts: The same guide does not give contour instructions for the brow bone and no study compares shading with brightening [3].

claims.claim: A natural look needs soft contrast and thorough blending
claims.believers: A men's contouring guide warns that harsh lines and over-blending can undermine the look and recommends less contrast for everyday wear [4].
claims.experts: Wikipedia's eyeshadow article names blending as the most important application step [6].

claims.claim: Makeup is a reversible alternative to brow-bone surgery
claims.believers: Appearance-forum posters discuss brow-bone implants and brow tilt at length, and makeup is the temporary way to try a deeper-set look.
claims.experts: Eyeshadow is removed with makeup remover or soap and water [6]; whether it changes how others rate the face has not been studied.

claims.claim: Eyeshadow around the eye is low risk
claims.believers: Users describe it as removable and low commitment.
claims.experts: Wikipedia notes fragrances and preservatives as common cosmetic allergens and the eye-area skin as thin and sensitive; US cosmetics need no pre-market FDA approval except colour additives [5].
